title: In a meeting
topic: taking the floor, making proposals, wrapping up
why: Last step of the work unit: the learner takes part in a meeting, takes the floor, makes proposals, agrees or disagrees, then wraps up. The lesson reuses the conditional and the connectors already seen, and locks in estar de acuerdo, tener razón and proponer + infinitive before the subjunctive arrives.

Opening the meeting and taking the floor

A meeting in Spanish follows the same pattern as in English: you open it, discuss the items on the agenda (el orden del día), make decisions and wrap up. To open:

  • Bueno, ¿empezamos? (Okay, shall we start?)
  • El objetivo de la reunión es… (The goal of the meeting is…)
  • Hoy vamos a hablar de tres puntos. (Today we're going to discuss three items.)

Taking the floor politely

SpanishEnglish
Si me permitís, …If I may, …
Perdona, ¿puedo decir una cosa?Sorry, can I say something?
Quería añadir que…I wanted to add that…
Me gustaría comentar algo.I'd like to comment on something.
Una pregunta: …A question: …

Quería (imperfect) and me gustaría (conditional) soften the request, exactly like \"I wanted to…\" and \"I'd like to…\" in English.

Vosotros around the table

English has just one \"you,\" but in Spain, when you speak to several coworkers, you use vosotros (a bit like \"you all\" or \"you guys\"), even in a meeting: ¿Qué os parece? (What do you all think?), ¿Estáis de acuerdo?, ¿Tenéis alguna pregunta?, Si me permitís… People keep ustedes for very formal settings, and in Latin America it's the only plural form.

Learn to spot the vosotros endings: tenéis, estáis, podéis, permitís, and the pronoun os: ¿Qué os parece?

", "

Proposing, agreeing, disagreeing

Proponer + noun or infinitive

Proponer (to propose, to suggest) is conjugated like poner:

Personproponer
yopropongo
túpropones
él, ella, ustedpropone
nosotros, nosotrasproponemos
vosotros, vosotrasproponéis
ellos, ellas, ustedesproponen

For now, follow it with a noun or an infinitive: Propongo una pausa. Propongo cambiar la fecha. The construction propongo que… + conjugated verb (\"I suggest that we…\") requires the subjunctive, a special verb form you'll learn soon.

Other ways to make a suggestion, which you already know: Podríamos… (We could…), Deberíamos… (We should…), ¿Y si…?, ¿Por qué no…?

Agreeing or not

To agreeTo disagree
Estoy de acuerdo (contigo, con Marta).No estoy de acuerdo.
Tienes razón.Yo no lo veo así.
Me parece bien. / Me parece buena idea.No sé, yo creo que es demasiado caro.
¡Exacto!Tienes razón en parte, pero…

The big trap: \"I agree\" is not a verb in Spanish but estar + de acuerdo, never with ser: Estoy de acuerdo. And \"to be right\" is tener razón (word for word \"to have reason\"), with no article: Tienes razón.

", "

Wrapping up and dividing the work

To close a discussion, you sum up, check there are no more questions and assign the tasks.

SpanishEnglish
En resumen, …To sum up, …
Entonces, quedamos en enviar el informe el lunes.So, we've agreed to send the report on Monday.
Laura se encarga de llamar al cliente.Laura will take care of calling the client.
¿Alguna pregunta? ¿Alguna duda?Any questions?
Si no hay más preguntas, terminamos aquí.If there are no more questions, let's wrap up here.
Para terminar, gracias a todos por venir.Finally, thank you all for coming.

Quedar en + infinitive means \"to agree to\": Hemos quedado en vernos el lunes. Don't confuse it with quedar on its own (to meet up) or with quedarse (to stay).

After the meeting, someone writes up el acta (the minutes). It's a feminine noun, but it takes el in the singular because it starts with a stressed a, like el agua: el acta, las actas.

En resumen: este año vamos a la feria con un espacio más pequeño y Lucía se encarga de la reserva. ¿Alguna pregunta?To sum up: this year we're going to the trade fair with a smaller space, and Lucía will take care of the booking. Any questions?

The connectors you already know give structure to what you say: primero, además, entonces, al final. With en resumen and para terminar, you'll instantly sound more professional.
